The advertising claim's uncertainty metadata is stale: footnote 4 and surrounding marketing paragraphs are supplied. The external Advertising Guidelines and their supplementary FAQs and guidance remain missing.

The external Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010 are missing. Can their applicable versions be supplied to verify gift, discount and product-type classifications? No supplied dependency IDs identify them.

Scope placement changes observable answers. For a known distributor and an unoffered component, node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE, while node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b can return FALSE. Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and both offer-level candidates similarly place promotional linkage in scope. Whether these cases should return not caught or OUT_OF_SCOPE remains unresolved.

Node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 returns OUT_OF_SCOPE for an unlinked benefit rather than TRUE for satisfaction of the selected gift control. An unknown scope also returns UNKNOWN even when a known non-gift or discount would settle the corresponding unrestricted Boolean expression. These are runtime distinctions, not source-established legal restrictions.

Both offer-level candidates combine offer-level promotional linkage with existence of a non-discount gift. Unless supplied classifications establish that the same gift participates in the linked promotion, a mixed offer could be overclassified. Whether an offer-wide link establishes that connection remains unresolved.

Node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 leaves component enumeration and evidential completeness implicit. Its existential fact requires sufficient evidence before FALSE can establish that no offered component qualifies. Generic UNKNOWN semantics do not validate an externally supplied FALSE.

The discount exception and TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT concern only the selected gift control. Neither establishes overall legality. Section 103 authorisation or exemption is likewise not a stated exception to the gift restriction.

The source says guaranteed returns or incentives may be gifts, and distinguishes fund returns from distributor top-ups. Automatic gift classification would add an unsupported restriction; blanket exemption would add an unsupported permission. The candidates generally retain classification as supplied judgment.

Node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b focuses on the offeror independently of funding or fulfilment. The source supports offering as the trigger, but does not resolve disputed attribution, agency or third-party arrangements.

The circular defines distributors within SFC-authorised fund distribution, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 refers to investment products generally. Fund-specific predicates may fit the selected circular context; equivalence to the full underlying Code provision is not established.

The supplied units do not establish a concrete effective interval. The FAQ date identifies a referenced document, not the effective date of every rule. Applicable versions and competing temporal interpretations remain unresolved.
